# SB-1039 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
- Stored hydraulic energy in hydraulic cylinders, accumulators, and pressurized manifolds associated with machining heat treat furnace handling and tooling presents a release hazard during maintenance, tooling changeover, and furnace cycling. A sudden release can cause uncontrolled motion of handling arms, platen drop, unexpected clamp release, and pressurized fluid spray. Injuries observed in related incidents include crush, impact, and laceration, and near-miss events have been traced to residual charge retained after isolation procedures. Investigation found that procedural gaps and incomplete verification of energy-zero status were common contributors. The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C; although thermal controls are outside the scope of hydraulic energy control, thermal cycling affects hydraulic component stress and seals, which can influence stored energy behavior and leak potential.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P2-L3-HT02 and all peripheral hydraulic fixtures, actuators, hoses, valves, and isolation devices used for part handling, clamping, and heat treat load/unload within line P2-L3. This includes portable jacks, mobile carts with hydraulic actuators, and any temporary hydraulic connections used during tooling setup in the P2-L3 area. Personnel working on electrical, mechanical, and process controls for the furnace and associated handling systems are also within the affected group.

Required controls
- All work that could expose personnel to stored hydraulic energy on EQ-P2-L3-HT02 and associated systems must follow the lockout-tagout requirements in QS-PROC-09 and the isolation verification procedures in SOP-P2-L3-04. Before any maintenance or tooling changeover, the following controls are mandatory:
  - De-pressurize hydraulic supply and isolate energy sources in accordance with QS-PROC-09. Use isolation points identified in the equipment drawings and in SOP-P2-L3-04.
  - Physically block or mechanically restrain moving elements where practical after de-pressurization to prevent motion from residual charge or external forces. Use manufacturer-recommended blocks or fixtures designed for the specific actuator geometry.
  - Bleed and relieve trapped fluid from downstream lines and actuators using the bleed ports and drain points documented in EQ-P2-L3-HT02 maintenance records. Confirm fluid discharge is controlled to a safe collection point to prevent slips and environmental release.
  - Verify zero-energy state by performing independent validation steps: operate local controls to confirm no movement, measure downstream pressure with calibrated gauges if used per SOP-P2-L3-04, and conduct a physical inspection of locking devices and blocks.
  - Tag and document all isolated lines and devices with the responsible technician’s identification and the maintenance task reference. Tags must reference the work order and must remain in place until all verifications and restoration steps are complete.
  - Use only rated personal protective equipment for hydraulic fluid exposure and potential pinch points, and ensure at least one designated observer is present when releasing any stored energy.
  - Do not rely solely on visual valve position indicators where concealed pressure traps are possible. Follow the sequences in SOP-P2-L3-04 for bleed and verification.
  - When testing or cycling is required post-maintenance, re-energize gradually and from a safe control location, with personnel clear of motion zones. Observe for leaks, unusual noises, or unexpected motion before proceeding with full system pressurization.

Background and step rationale
- Residual hydraulic pressure can be trapped in downstream circuits by check valves, pilot-operated valves, or actuator end-of-stroke geometries. Thermal expansion from furnace cycles, including at the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) of 845 °C, can change fluid volume and pressure in connected components if not isolated or bled. The controls above reduce the risk of inadvertent motion and fluid release by addressing isolation, controlled venting, mechanical blocking, and independent verification. Documented verification provides an auditable trail for safety compliance and incident investigation. The requirement to follow QS-PROC-09 and SOP-P2-L3-04 ensures consistency with system-wide lockout and P2-L3-specific practices. Reference SB-1023 for recent incident learnings that informed the verification and mechanical blocking emphasis in this bulletin.

Examples
- Example scenarios illustrating required controls:
  - Tooling changeout on a hydraulic gripper: After isolating the hydraulic supply, bleed downstream lines at the tool quick-disconnect, install mechanical blocks on the gripper, and perform a push test at the tool handle to confirm no motion before removing fixtures.
  - Cylinder replacement: Isolate and tag the supply, open the cylinder bleed plug to relieve trapped charge to a collection container, install external retaining hardware to prevent piston movement, and log the bleed event in the maintenance record per SOP-P2-L3-04 instructions.

Records to keep
- Maintain a copy of the isolation tag and verification checklist attached to the corresponding work order. Record the following in the maintenance history for EQ-P2-L3-HT02: equipment isolation point identifiers, bleed port used, name of technician performing verification, reference to QS-PROC-09 and SOP-P2-L3-04 procedures followed, and any observed anomalies. Retain photographic evidence of mechanical blocking and bleed discharge where practicable. Any deviations or incidents must be reported and documented according to SB-1023 and escalated to the P2-L3 maintenance supervisor.

Compliance and training
- All staff assigned to work on EQ-P2-L3-HT02 must review SOP-P2-L3-04 and the lockout-tagout requirements in QS-PROC-09. Supervisors must ensure that job planning includes the required controls described here and that records are completed for each maintenance activity.

Effective date
- Effective date: Rev B (implementation upon release of this revision)

Related documents
- QS-PROC-09  
- SB-1023  
- SOP-P2-L3-04
